stem:
A 45-year-old man with nephrotic syndrome has a markedly decreased plasma albumin concentration and develops generalized edema.

Which of the following changes in capillary exchange forces most directly explains the accumulation of interstitial fluid in this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Decreased blood colloid osmotic pressure reduces venous-end reabsorption
options.misconception: None; albumin loss lowers the osmotic force that pulls fluid back into capillaries.
options.explanation: Net reabsorption occurs near the venous end because blood colloid osmotic pressure (BCOP) exceeds capillary hydrostatic pressure there; hypoalbuminemia lowers BCOP, so reabsorption fails and fluid accumulates.

options.label: B
options.text: Increased interstitial hydrostatic pressure opposes filtration
options.misconception: A force that limits edema is being named as its cause.
options.explanation: Rising interstitial hydrostatic pressure opposes further filtration and would limit, not cause, fluid accumulation.

options.label: C
options.text: Increased capillary hydrostatic pressure increases filtration at the arterial end
options.misconception: The hydrostatic limb is being blamed in a disorder of the osmotic limb.
options.explanation: Nephrotic albumin loss does not raise capillary hydrostatic pressure; the driving change is the fall in colloid osmotic pressure.

options.label: D
options.text: Decreased capillary permeability limits protein return
options.misconception: The renal protein loss is being attributed to capillary walls.
options.explanation: The protein is lost through the kidney, not the peripheral capillaries; capillary permeability is not decreased, and the edema reflects low plasma oncotic pressure.

options.label: E
options.text: Increased lymphatic drainage removes excess fluid
options.misconception: A compensatory drainage pathway is being mistaken for the cause of accumulation.
options.explanation: Lymphatic drainage removes unreabsorbed fluid and would mitigate edema; the accumulation occurs because reduced oncotic pressure overwhelms that drainage.

context: Learning objective: apply Starling forces to edema. Filtration occurs where hydrostatic pressure exceeds colloid osmotic pressure; reabsorption occurs where osmotic pressure dominates, so hypoalbuminemia causes edema.
